sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Lake County, Florida?
sections.html:
The Lake County Tax Collector mails and collects the bills, while the Lake County Property Appraiser sets the value those bills rest on. Keep that split in mind when something looks wrong, because each office can only fix its own part.

The tax collector's property tax page says any change to a name, mailing address, location or assessed value on the roll must go through the property appraiser, whose number it prints as (352) 253-2150. The collector's page also says collection must begin on November 1 for the tax year that runs January through December, and that the owner carries the duty to make sure the bill gets paid even if no notice arrives. If a mortgage company pays through escrow, the page says an escrow code appears at the top of the notice and a banner at the bottom.

  • Property Appraiser: values every parcel, handles homestead and other exemption filings, mails the August notice of proposed taxes.
  • Tax Collector: prints and mails the bill, takes payment, runs the June tax certificate sale on unpaid accounts.
  • Clerk of the Circuit Court: records the deed and collects documentary stamp tax when a sale closes, and staffs the value adjustment board.

sections.h2: What are the Lake County early payment discounts and deadlines?
sections.html:
Lake County lets owners save up to 4 percent by paying in November, and the discount shrinks by one point each month through February. The gross amount is due by March 31, and April 1 starts delinquency.

Lake County tax collector payment schedule, as printed on the collector's property tax page
Paid in full byDiscount
November 304 percent
December 313 percent
January 312 percent
February 281 percent
March 31Gross amount, no discount

A payment sent by mail earns the discount according to its postmark. On April 1 the page says a 3 percent statutory interest charge is added to the total due. The state lists the same ladder statewide and adds that tax certificates are sold on unpaid items by June 1.

Ask the tax collector's office about installment plans and the tax certificate sale schedule before you rely on either, since the collector's office sets those details each year.

sections.h2: What millage rates apply to a Lake County home?
sections.html:
It depends on where the house sits. The Lake County Property Appraiser's 2026 final millage rate sheet lists a separate total for every taxing district code, and the totals run from the low 13s for unincorporated land to the high 19s in some cities.

For the unincorporated codes at the top of the sheet, the totals printed are 13.0632, 13.0670 and 13.4678 depending on the code. The county general fund line is 5.0254 in every row, the school board state line is 3.0560, and the school board local line is 2.9980. Those lines repeat across the sheet, so the gap between districts comes from the extra lines: the city levy, a fire or ambulance district, a hospital district and community development districts.

  • Clermont: 16.2875 total, with a city line of 4.2000.
  • Leesburg: 15.8704 total, with a city line of 3.3783.
  • Mount Dora: 18.7921 total, with a city line of 6.3000.
  • Eustis: 19.8819 total, with a city line of 7.3898.
  • Montverde: 15.3975 total, with a city line of 2.8300.

Read the sheet for your own code before you assume any figure. The code is on your tax notice and on the appraiser's parcel record. Lake County's municipalities on the sheet include Astatula, Clermont, Eustis, Fruitland Park, Groveland, Howey-in-the-Hills, Lady Lake, Leesburg, Mascotte, Minneola, Montverde, Mount Dora, Tavares and Umatilla.

sections.h2: How do homestead exemption and Save Our Homes work for Lake County owners?
sections.html:
A Lake County homeowner who lives in the house on January 1 can file for homestead by March 1, and the state revenue department says the exemption is up to $50,000. The first $25,000 reaches all taxes including school taxes, and the second layer of up to $25,000 applies to value above $50,000 and to non-school taxes only.

The form is DR-501, filed with the property appraiser. Renting the home or moving out ends the exemption. The Lake County Property Appraiser's home page links a list of exemptions and how to qualify, which is the place to check senior, veteran and disability benefits that local rules may add.

Save Our Homes limits yearly growth of the assessed value on a homestead to the lower of 3 percent or the change in the consumer price index. The Department of Revenue chart shows a 2026 cap of 2.7 percent, 2.9 percent for 2025 and 3.0 percent for 2024. A sale resets the property to just value the following January 1, so the buyer's bill can differ sharply from the seller's. Portability lets a seller carry the benefit to a new Florida homestead if it is established within three years of January 1 of the year the old one was abandoned, using Form DR-501T.

sections.h2: What happens to Lake County property tax when you sell the house?
sections.html:
Current-year tax is split between seller and buyer at closing, and any back tax has to be gone before title passes. Expect the title company to pay the collector out of the seller's share.

Because bills arrive in November for a calendar year and are paid in arrears, a house sold in spring or summer normally has no current bill yet. The title agent estimates it. Get the exact amount and any older balance from the collector while the contract is still being negotiated.

  • Pull the parcel record from the appraiser and confirm the owner and mailing address.
  • Ask the collector whether any year is delinquent or holds a certificate.
  • Tell the title company if you have a homestead exemption so the proration uses the right figure.
  • Plan for the buyer's value reset after closing, since the next bill can be higher.

Deed stamps are set by statute at 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and each party stays liable even if the contract assigns the cost to one side.

sections.h2: What if Lake County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquency starts April 1, and the property can eventually reach a tax deed sale. Under Florida's statutes a tax certificate holder may apply for a tax deed after two years have elapsed since April 1 of the year the certificate was issued.

The certificate sale opens on or before June 1. The statute has the collector award each certificate to the bidder who accepts the lowest interest rate, bidding down in quarter-percent steps, and certificates nobody wants go to the county. A homestead parcel with less than $250 delinquent is issued to the county instead of auctioned. After the application, the clerk holds the public auction, and the high bidder posts a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is greater.

Owners who cannot pay can look at the homestead tax deferral. A deferral application goes to the tax collector on Form DR-570 by March 31 after the assessment year, and it covers the part of the tax that exceeds 5 percent of household income, or 3 percent for an owner 65 or older. Installment prepayment requests must reach the collector by May 1 of the assessment year.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Lake County value?
sections.html:
Look at the August notice of proposed taxes, and if the value looks wrong, file a petition with the clerk's value adjustment board within 25 days of that notice. The state revenue department's taxpayer page prints that 25-day window.

Denials of an exemption, classification, portability or deferral run on a separate clock: the petition deadline is 30 days counted from the mailing date of the denial letter. The board is staffed through the Lake County clerk's office, which publishes its own forms page. Talk to the appraiser first, since many questions about square footage or exemption status resolve before any petition.

Taxing authorities hold public hearings on their budgets in September and October and adopt final millage after that. Those hearings are where you can speak about rates, as opposed to the value of your own house.

faqs.q: When are Lake County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills go out in November and the full amount is due by March 31, with discounts of 4, 3, 2 and 1 percent for paying by the end of November, December, January and February. Anything unpaid is delinquent on April 1, and the collector's page says a 3 percent charge is added then.

faqs.q: Who do I call to change my Lake County mailing address on a tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Lake County Property Appraiser, not the tax collector. The collector's page says name, address, location and assessed value changes are made by the appraiser, and it lists (352) 253-2150 for that office.

faqs.q: What is the total millage in unincorporated Lake County?
faqs.a: The 2026 final millage sheet prints 13.0632, 13.0670 or 13.4678 for unincorporated codes, depending on the district. Your notice shows your code, and the sheet shows the full line breakdown.

faqs.q: Does selling my Lake County house reset my tax value?
faqs.a: Yes for the buyer. Florida's Department of Revenue says a sale is a change of ownership and the property goes to just value the following January 1, which ends any Save Our Homes cap built up under the seller.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Lake County house with unpaid property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance, plus any certificate redemption, comes out of the seller's proceeds. Collect the payoff number from the collector's office and hand it to the closing agent early.
